why: It uses the public 46-letter dataset (90 images per letter) that most Modi papers test on, and it says VGG16 does better on letters that look alike.
take: The claim that similar letters are where models differ, which is what we set out to measure.
differ: They say it improves on similar letters but give no numbers for them. We report mistakes pair by pair, before and after our change, including the pairs that get worse.

why: It's the best recent CNN result on the same dataset, and it says look-alike letters are the hardest part. Its attention layer is also the closest idea to ours: look harder at the strokes that matter.
take: The idea that a model should focus on the strokes that tell similar letters apart.
differ: They use one attention layer for every letter and never list which letters get confused. We list the confused pairs and build a separate specialist for each one, looking at the regions SHAP picks for that pair.

why: It's the only paper that tests an SVM and CNNs on the same Modi images, and it reports just 77% for the SVM.
take: The SVM as a starting point, and its 77% as the number to beat.
differ: They don't describe any specific handcrafted features for their SVM. We give the SVM proper features (HOG, Zernike moments and LBP).

why: It's the closest earlier work using classical classifiers for Modi, on features taken from VGG16.
take: The idea that a classical classifier can do well on Modi if the features are good.
differ: Features from VGG16 can't be pointed at on the character. We use handcrafted features, so SHAP can show which part of a letter separates a pair.

why: An early Modi recogniser that uses Otsu thresholding, and it found that similar-shaped letters do worst.
take: Otsu thresholding as our main cleaning step, and the finding about similar shapes.
differ: They used 22 letters with 8 images each and stop at the observation. We use all 57 classes on a public dataset and do something about the similar shapes.

why: It shows Zernike moments describe Modi shapes better than Hu moments (86.7% vs 70%).
take: Zernike moments as one of our features.
differ: They only tested 100 digit images. We use all 57 classes.
